source: Ed4 J.4.1.1 and J.4.1.2, pp.J-5 to J-8; C.4.15, p.C-56; Ed4 L, p.L-17 and Table L-1, p.L-18
description: WTRP D_PDUs to a broadcast address and to another node draw no WARNING, but the analysis reports WTRP in use to each bound client, once, and a token EOW in a later transmission does not repeat the report.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ (service type tx_mode 2, no confirmation) and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED with MTU 2048 (A-0041, A-0047). Conn 2 connects and never binds. At 2000, from 0.0.1.3, EOW 0, EOT 10: an EXTENSION extended type 3 (TABLE) to the broadcast address 15.255.255.255, address size 7, and an EXTENSION extended type 1 (INVITE) to another node, 0.0.1.9, address size 4. Neither is addressed to this node individual address, so neither draws a WARNING (J-0053 and C-0735 coordinator ruling, C-0394). The analysis still reads them (J-0043, J-0083): at the burst end 3000 it reports WTRP in use by 0.0.1.3, once for the burst, to conn 1 only, since conn 2 is not bound (J-0082). Report: S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION (type 19) to every bound client, MSG TYPE 1, 9-byte MSG BODY: finding code, the node (4 bytes), the addressee of the WARNING behind it or 0 (4 bytes), addresses 28-bit most significant first (J-0082). Nothing is queued, so the MAC starts no timer (K-0096). At 10000 a burst from 0.0.1.3 with a PADDING to 0.0.1.9 carrying EOW 0xD01, the WTRP token (EOW type 13, J-0070, Ed4 L p.L-17): more WTRP evidence, but WTRP is already the last mode reported for 0.0.1.3, so nothing is reported (J-0082).
